summary: Iteration 10 backend regression PASSED for the deployment-readiness scope (15/16 tests green). Verified: (a) NEW DELETE /api/auth/me — admin self-delete correctly blocked with HTTP 400 'Admin accounts cannot self-delete', regular user delete returns {ok:true}, subsequent GET /api/auth/me returns 401, order is retained but anonymised (user_id starts with 'deleted_', shipping_name and shipping_phone both '[deleted]'); (b) Admin seed still works — POST /api/auth/login as admin@garlic.app / Admin@123 returns 200 with role='admin' and /auth/me confirms role, so removing the source-code ADMIN_* defaults did NOT break seeding since /app/backend/.env still holds real values; (c) Razorpay LIVE test-mode regression — POST /api/orders/create returns mock=false, key_id matches backend .env, order.razorpay_order_id starts with 'order_'; HMAC-SHA256(RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET, '{oid}|{payment_id}') verify flips status to 'paid' and awards int(round(amount*0.1)) Nest Points; replaying the same verify is idempotent (points balance unchanged); bad signature is rejected (400) and the order stays 'created'; (d) baseline regression — GET /api/products, /api/categories, /api/editorials, /api/points, POST /api/products/{id}/reviews, admin PUT /api/admin/orders/{id}/status invalid-transition rejection (created→delivered → 400). ONE CRITICAL BUG DETECTED in the new DELETE /api/auth/me endpoint: it targets the WRONG Mongo collections for wishlist and points ledger — server.py:490 does `db.wishlists.delete_many(...)` but the real collection populated by POST /api/wishlist/toggle is `db.wishlist` (singular, see server.py:874-878); server.py:489 does `db.points_history.delete_many(...)` but the real points collection is `db.user_points` (see server.py:713, 725, 743). Direct MongoDB probe confirmed 1 wishlist doc and 1 user_points doc leaked for the deleted user. This is an Apple App Store 5.1.1(v) compliance blocker — the endpoint advertises full personal-data purge but does not purge the wishlist or the Nest Points ledger. Razorpay secrets read from /app/backend/.env for HMAC only and were NOT written to the report.

critical.issue: Personal data leak on account delete: wishlist items and Nest Points ledger are NOT purged. server.py:490 targets `db.wishlists` (plural) but real collection is `db.wishlist` (see server.py:865-878). server.py:489 targets `db.points_history` but real collection is `db.user_points` (see server.py:713, 725, 743). Direct Mongo probe test_iteration10_delete_leak_probe.py:test_delete_purges_wishlist_and_points confirmed 1 wishlist doc + 1 user_points doc left behind after DELETE returned 200. Apple 5.1.1(v) compliance risk.

minor.issue: Endpoint also targets `db.interactions.delete_many({user_id})` — confirmed collection exists (server.py:771) so this line is OK. Just noting: no admin GET /api/admin/orders/{id} exists (only list endpoint), so post-delete admin verification of anonymised order requires filtering the list. Not a bug, just an API gap; iteration 10 tests worked around it by filtering /api/admin/orders.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:485-490 — delete_many collection names DO NOT match the collections written elsewhere in the same file. `db.wishlists` (plural, delete side) vs `db.wishlist` (singular, everywhere else). `db.points_history` (delete side) vs `db.user_points` (points award/spend/read). Pre-shipping this to Apple review would fail 5.1.1(v). Add integration coverage that (a) seeds a wishlist item, (b) awards points, (c) calls DELETE /api/auth/me, (d) asserts both collections have 0 docs for that user_id.

server.py:33-34 — ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_MOBILE/ADMIN_PASSWORD now default to empty string. Startup emits `logger.warning('Admin seed skipped: ADMIN_EMAIL/... not fully configured')` if any is missing. Good defensive posture; if a fresh deploy accidentally clears the env, admin login will simply fail rather than seed a default 'admin/admin' credential. Verified admin login still works because /app/backend/.env still holds real values.

server.py:493-496 — Order anonymisation is a partial redaction; ship-address is retained (only name+phone masked). That is likely intentional (address may be legally required for accounting) but if privacy team wants full anonymisation, also mask `shipping_address`. Consider redacting the phone number to a hash if you want irreversibility (current `[deleted]` is fine for audit).

server.py:475-500 — No token-invalidation step. Because tokens are JWTs signed with the current secret and carry `id/name/email/mobile/role`, and get_current_user does `db.users.find_one({id})`, once the user record is deleted `get_current_user` will 401 on the next call (verified). Good — no server-side blacklist needed as long as get_current_user does the DB lookup (it does, at server.py's Depends chain).
server.py:483 — Correct admin guard order (role check BEFORE any deletion) so a mis-attempted admin self-delete cannot corrupt admin-owned rows. Verified with test_admin_cannot_self_delete.

rca_of_issue: RCA of the delete-endpoint leak bug: the new DELETE /api/auth/me handler (server.py:475-500) was written without cross-referencing the actual Mongo collection names used elsewhere in server.py. The developer assumed pluralised collection names (`wishlists`, `points_history`) whereas the rest of the codebase uses `wishlist` (singular, see server.py:865-879) and `user_points` (server.py:711-747). Because Motor lazily creates a collection on first write, the delete_many() call on the wrong name silently succeeds with 0 matches — no exception, no log, no failing test. Reproduction: (1) signup a fresh user, (2) POST /api/wishlist/toggle with any product_id, (3) DELETE /api/auth/me (200), (4) direct Mongo query `db.wishlist.count_documents({user_id: uid})` still returns 1. Mitigation: change line 490 to `await db.wishlist.delete_many({'user_id': uid})` and line 489 to `await db.user_points.delete_many({'user_id': uid})`. After the fix, run `pytest tests/test_iteration10_delete_leak_probe.py` — should pass. Also add a `_USER_COLLECTIONS = ['wishlist','shortlists','reviews','interactions','user_points']` constant near the top of server.py and iterate it in delete_account() so future collection additions are hard to forget.
